label: Secretory_Carcinoma
answer_markdown:
## Key Facts

- Most cases arise in the parotid gland; can also occur in minor or submandibular glands.
- Features a pathognomonic ETV6 gene rearrangement, usually ETV6::NTRK3 fusion.
- Histology mimics secretory carcinoma of the breast, with microcystic, tubular, and solid patterns plus abundant secretions.
- IHC: Strong S100 and mammaglobin positivity; negative for DOG1, p63, and p40 (differentiates from acinic cell carcinoma).
- Generally low to intermediate grade malignant behavior; lymph node metastases can occur.
- Key DDx: Acinic cell carcinoma (no ETV6 rearrangement, DOG1+); salivary duct carcinoma (AR+, apocrine cytology, comedo necrosis).

## Terminology

- Secretory carcinoma (SC): A primary salivary gland malignancy defined by ETV6 rearrangement ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Secretory_Carcinoma.html)).
- Mammary analogue secretory carcinoma (MASC): Now not recommended, replaced by "secretory carcinoma".
- Abbreviations: SC.

## Essential and Desirable Diagnostic Criteria

- **Essential:**
  - Definitional ETV6 gene rearrangement (typically t(12;15)(p13;q25) ETV6::NTRK3 fusion) ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Secretory_Carcinoma.html); [Hn Cardesa](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Cardesa.pdf#page=260)).
  - Architectural features: Lobulated growth with microcystic, tubular, papillary, and solid areas containing abundant eosinophilic or bubbly secretions ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Secretory_Carcinoma.html); [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsmalignant.html)).
  - Tumor cells: Bland nuclei, vesicular chromatin, mild to moderate atypia, distinct nucleoli, and intraluminal/colloid-like secretions ([PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsmalignant.html)).
  - IHC: Strong S100 and mammaglobin positivity, negative DOG1, p63, and p40 ([Hn Cardesa](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Cardesa.pdf#page=260)).
- **Desirable:**
  - Histological resemblance to breast secretory carcinoma ([Hn Cardesa](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Cardesa.pdf#page=260)).
  - Identification of papilliform, cribriform, or cystic patterns ([Hn Oral](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Oral.pdf#page=311)).
  - Cytology showing papillary or sheet-like fragments with occasional multinucleation ([PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsmalignant.html)).

## Etiology/Pathogenesis

- Balanced t(12;15)(p13;q25) chromosomal translocation leads to ETV6::NTRK3 fusion gene ([Hn Cardesa](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Cardesa.pdf#page=260)).
  - This genetic signature is characteristic and required for diagnosis.
- Tumor cells resemble intercalated duct cells, lacking serous acinar PAS-positive granules.

## Clinical Issues

- **Epidemiology:**
  - Rare tumor; most occur in the parotid gland, followed by submandibular and minor salivary glands ([Hn Cardesa](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Cardesa.pdf#page=260); [Hn Oral](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Oral.pdf#page=311)).
- **Presentation:**
  - Typically presents as a painless mass, frequently single-nodular ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Secretory_Carcinoma.html); [Hn Oral](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Oral.pdf#page=311)).
- **Natural History/Behavior:**
  - Generally low to intermediate grade; can show nodal involvement ([PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsmalignant.html)).
  - Higher rate of nodal disease compared to typical salivary acinic cell carcinoma.
  - Prognosis is generally favorable with complete surgical excision ([Hn Oral](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Oral.pdf#page=311)).
- **Prognosis:**
  - Most patients do well; late local recurrence or metastasis is possible.

## Macroscopic

- Usually appears as a well-circumscribed, lobulated, or multinodular mass ([Hn Oral](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Oral.pdf#page=311)).
- May be cystic or solid.
- Cut surface may show cystic spaces filled with secretions.
- Areas of secondary infarction after FNA or cyst content reaction can be present
  - ![Secretory carcinoma secondary changes](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-public-figures-830130787988/textbook_figures_web_v1/hn_thompson/hn_thompson_p0360_fig02_figure_13_60.jpg)
- Additional images:
  - ![Cystic tumor](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsmammarygupta07.jpg)
  - ![Solid tumor](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsmammarygupta09.jpg)
  - ![Macrocystic lesion](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsmammarygupta15.jpg)

## Microscopic

- Growth is lobulated; multiple growth patterns present in most tumors ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Secretory_Carcinoma.html); [Hn Cardesa](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Cardesa.pdf#page=260)), including:
  - Microcystic, tubular, papillary, solid, and cribriform nests.
  - Multiple patterns often found in the same tumor.
  - Cystic, macrocystic, and papilliform areas documented.
- Tumor cells:
  - Bland, often eccentrically placed nuclei, vesicular chromatin, distinct nucleoli, mild pleomorphism ([PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsmalignant.html)).
  - Abundant eosinophilic or bubbly cytoplasm, sometimes vacuolated.
- Secretions:
  - Abundant intraluminal eosinophilic, PAS-positive, diastase-resistant secretory material.
  - Colloid-like accumulations often noted ([PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsmalignant.html)).
- Images:
  - ![Solid and cystic architecture](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsmammarygupta13.jpg)
  - ![Colloid-like secretions](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsmammarygupta17.jpg)
  - ![Papilliform architecture](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsmammarygupta16.jpg)

## Ancillary Tests

- **Immunohistochemistry:**
  - S100: diffusely and strongly positive ([Hn Cardesa](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Cardesa.pdf#page=260); ![S100](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsmammarygupta22.jpg)).
  - Mammaglobin: positive ([Hn Cardesa](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Cardesa.pdf#page=260)).
  - DOG1: negative (contrasts with acinic cell carcinoma).
  - p63/p40: negative (contrasts with other carcinomas).
  - MUC4: positive (![MUC4](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsmammarygupta23.jpg)).
- **Molecular:**
  - ETV6 rearrangement, typically ETV6::NTRK3 fusion, is diagnostic ([Hn Cardesa](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Cardesa.pdf#page=260); [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Secretory_Carcinoma.html)).

## Differential Diagnosis

- **Acinic Cell Carcinoma ([Hn Cardesa](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Cardesa.pdf#page=260))**
  - AciCC shows PAS-positive cytoplasmic zymogen granules, not seen in secretory carcinoma.
  - AciCC is DOG1+ and S100/mammaglobin negative, while secretory carcinoma is S100+/mammaglobin+ and DOG1-.
  - ETV6 rearrangement (secretory carcinoma) is absent in AciCC.
- **Myoepithelial Carcinoma ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/HN/Mucinous_Adenocarcinoma.html))**
  - S100 and calponin or SMA positive; can show nested/corded patterns but lacks ETV6 rearrangement.
- **Salivary Duct Carcinoma ([Hn Oral](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/source_pdfs/HN_Oral.pdf#page=311); [PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandssalivaryductcarcinoma.html))**
  - High-grade cytology, comedo necrosis, and apocrine features (apocrine cytology, androgen receptor+).
  - Typically AR+, while secretory carcinoma is AR-.
  - Does not have the ETV6::NTRK3 fusion.
- **Mucoepidermoid Carcinoma ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/HN/Mucinous_Adenocarcinoma.html))**
  - Mixture of epidermoid, intermediate, and mucus cells.
  - Can be p63/p40 positive.
- **Sclerosing Polycystic Adenoma ([PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandssclerosingpolycysticadenoma.html))**
  - Benign, with preservation of lobular architecture and bilayered ducts/acini; no ETV6 rearrangement.
- **Sialadenoma Papilliferum ([PathOutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandssialadenoma.html))**
  - Biphasic tumor with exophytic squamous and endophytic glandular components; lacks ETV6 rearrangement.
- **Mucinous Adenocarcinoma ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/HN/Mucinous_Adenocarcinoma.html))**
  - Should exclude secretory carcinoma, acinic cell carcinoma, myoepithelial carcinoma, and metastatic mucinous tumors by morphology and IHC.
  - Typically negative for S100/mammaglobin and lacks ETV6 rearrangement.

cards.excerpt: Entity: Mucinous adenocarcinoma Section: differential_diagnosis To diagnose MA, other mucin-producing salivary gland carcinomas must be excluded, including mucin-rich mucoepidermoid carcinoma (epidermoid/intermediate cells; p63/p40+), mucinous and rhabdoid variants of salivary duct carcinoma (apocrine cytology; AR+), and the mucinous/secretory pattern of myoepithelial carcinoma (nested/corded pattern; S100, calponin, or SMA+). Metastasis from gastrointestinal, pancreaticobiliary, or lung adenocarcinomas should be ruled out clinically.

cards.excerpt: Fig. 21-18. Needle biopsy of parotid gland tumor diagnostic for carcinoma. A, Small tissue fragment showing a densely cellular proliferation (arrowhead) with scattered cells within fibroconnective tissue (arrows). B and C, Neoplastic cells in densely cellular area (B) and less cellular area (C) show moderate to marked nuclear pleomorphism with hyperchromatic nuclei. On the basis of the cytomorphologic features, the findings are those of a malignant undifferentiated neoplasm. Immunohistochemical staining showed the lesional cells to be reactive for (D) cytokeratin (AE1/AE3); (E) androgen receptor (nuclear); (F) GATA-3 (nuclear). The findings are diagnostic for salivary duct carcinoma (either occurring de novo or possibly the malignant component of a carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma). Radical excision of the tumor and neck dissection were subsequently performed confirming a diagnosis of a (de novo) salivary duct carcinoma with nodal metastasis.

cards.title: Secretory carcinoma — Essential features
cards.heading: Essential features
cards.text_excerpt:
Rare primary salivary gland carcinoma characterized by ETV6 gene rearrangement (Am J Surg Pathol 2010;34:599, Am J Surg Pathol 2020;44:1295, Am J Surg Pathol 2018;42:1121)
Predominantly (76%) occurs in parotid, minor salivary glands of oral cavity and submandibular gland
Also described in nasal cavity, skin and thyroid (Am J Surg Pathol 2020;44:1295)
Predominantly adults, wide age range (5 - 87 years) (Am J Surg Pathol 2020;44:1295, Histopathology 2012;61:387)
Various histological growth patterns, including cystic, solid, tubular, papillary cystic and lobular
Cysts with intraluminal colloid-like secretions (Am J Surg Pathol 2010;34:599)
Cells with bubbly cytoplasm and relatively monotonous round nuclei with small but distinct nucleoli (Am J Surg Pathol 2010;34:599, Histopathology 2012;61:387, Pathology 2015;47:659)
Immunohistochemical expression of GATA3, S100, NTRK3, MUC4, mammaglobin (Pathology 2015;47:659, Head Neck Pathol 2013;7:311, Histopathology 2020;76:375)
Generally low grade with indolent clinical behavior; however, local lymph node metastases may be seen in up to 22% (Histopathology 2012;61:387)
Rare high grade transformation with aggressive clinical behavior, including distant metastasis (Pathol Res Pract 2017;213:1112, Int J Surg Pathol 2017;25:613, Ann Oncol 2016;27:920)

cards.title: Secretory carcinoma — Clinical features
cards.heading: Clinical features
cards.text_excerpt:
Slow growing painless mass; mean duration: 1 year (Head Neck 2019;41:1227, Oral Oncol 2018;82:29)
Low T stage at diagnosis (almost always T1 or T2) (Oral Oncol 2018;82:29, Pathology 2015;47:659)
Generally indolent clinical course with recurrence rates of < 10% and 10 year overall survival of 95% after macroscopically complete resection (Head Neck 2019;41:1227)
Local lymph node involvement at diagnosis in a minority (5 - 22%) (JAMA Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2019;145:91, Histopathology 2012;61:387)
Distant metastases in < 5% (JAMA Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2019;145:91, Head Neck 2019;41:1227)
Locally aggressive behavior and poor outcomes have been reported if incompletely resected (Head Neck 2019;41:1227, Pathology 2015;47:659)
High grade transformation with aggressive clinical behavior including distant metastasis has been reported (Pathol Res Pract 2017;213:1112, Int J Surg Pathol 2017;25:613)

cards.title: Secretory carcinoma — Prognostic factors
cards.heading: Prognostic factors
cards.text_excerpt:
pT stage of 3 or 4 and high grade features appear most strongly associated with poor clinical outcomes (Head Neck 2019;41:1227, Pathology 2015;47:659)
While definite thresholds are not yet described, nuclear pleomorphism, easily identified mitotic activity or presence of comedonecrosis have been described to confer poor prognosis (Int J Clin Exp Pathol 2014;7:9008)
Rare high grade transformation with aggressive clinical behavior including distant metastasis has been reported (Am J Surg Pathol 2014;38:23, Am J Surg Pathol 2018;42:1121, Pathol Res Pract 2017;213:1112, Int J Surg Pathol 2017;25:613)

cards.title: Secretory carcinoma — Treatment
cards.heading: Treatment
cards.text_excerpt:
Primary resection
Neck dissection or adjuvant radiotherapy if adverse prognostic features or evidence of lymph node metastases present (JAMA Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2019;145:91, Pathol Res Pract 2017;213:1112, Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2021;164:27)
TRK inhibitors have shown promise in phase 1 and 2 trials for ETV6-NTRK3 rearranged tumors but efficacy is not established (N Engl J Med 2018;378:731)
Cases of initial response followed by acquired resistance have been reported in advanced disease (Ann Oncol 2016;27:920, Int J Surg Pathol 2017;25:613)

cards.title: Secretory carcinoma — Circumscribed or infiltrative edge
cards.heading: Circumscribed or infiltrative edge
cards.text_excerpt:
Lobulated architecture
Variable arrangements, including macrocystic, microcystic, solid, tubular, follicular and papillary cystic patterns (Am J Surg Pathol 2010;34:599, Am J Surg Pathol 2019;43:1483)
Pale eosinophilic colloid-like intraluminal secretions; secretions are periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) reagent positive and diastase resistant (Am J Surg Pathol 2010;34:599)
Tumor cells have eosinophilic or vacuolated cytoplasm and monomorphic round vesicular nuclei with small but distinctive nucleoli
Occasional lymphovascular invasion and perineural invasion are seen (Head Neck 2019;41:1227)
High grade transformation has been reported with a distinct population of tumor cells exhibiting solid or trabecular growth, infiltrative margins, desmoplastic stromal reaction, comedo-like necrosis, nuclear pleomorphism, increased mitotic rate, loss of secretory activity and perineural invasion
A distinct low grade (conventional) carcinomatous component is also present (Pathol Res Pract 2017;213:1112)
Microscopic (histologic) imagesContributed by Ruta Gupta, M.B.B.S., M.D.

Cytology is variable and nonspecific and requires high index of suspicion / awareness and cell block preparation
Difficult to distinguish from benign entities and other low grade malignancies (APMIS 2019;127:491, Acta Cytol 2017;61:469)
Cohesive clusters or sheets of epithelial cells with variable eosinophilic, granular to vacuolated cytoplasm and uniform nuclei with single nucleoli (APMIS 2019;127:491)
Papillary fragments and acinar arrangements commonly seen; cystic lesions may show cystic debris in the background (APMIS 2019;127:491, Diagn Cytopathol 2015;43:287)
Cell block preparation for immunohistochemistry with S100, GATA3, pan-TRK is useful (APMIS 2019;127:491, Cancer Cytopathol 2018;126:627)

Mammaglobin: 83% sensitive but lacks specificity in diagnostic context as it is expressed in intraductal carcinoma (86%) and polymorphous adenocarcinoma (37%) (Histopathology 2020 Sep 15 [Epub ahead of print])
Pan-TRK: nuclear staining is 64% sensitive and reported specificities range from 92% to 100% (Histopathology 2020;76:375, Histopathology 2019;75:54)
NB: cytoplasmic pan-TRK staining is extremely nonspecific and should be disregarded (Histopathology 2019;75:54)
Pan-TRK will not stain tumors with other fusion partners for ETV6 (Histopathology 2019;75:54, Am J Surg Pathol 2020;44:962)

cards.title: Secretory carcinoma — Molecular / cytogenetics description
cards.heading: Molecular / cytogenetics description
cards.text_excerpt:
Recurrent translocation t(12;15)(p13;q24), resulting in fusion of ETV6 on chromosome 12 and NTRK3 on chromosome 15 (Am J Surg Pathol 2010;34:599)
Alternate fusion partners have been identified, including ETV6-RET and ETV6-MET (Am J Surg Pathol 2020;44:1295, Hum Pathol 2019;83:50, Am J Surg Pathol 2018;42:1121)
Potential role of other non-ETV6 translocations according to recent reports: VIM-RET and CTNNA1-ALK (Am J Surg Pathol 2020;44:1295, Am J Surg Pathol 2020;44:962)
